title: A Consensus Glossary of Temporal Database Concepts
finding: Valid time and transaction time are established temporal database concepts; this study does not invent bitemporal modeling.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
finding: MemGPT studies virtual context management with hierarchical memory. It is related work, not an implemented baseline here.

title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
finding: Mem0 extracts, consolidates and retrieves memories and studies a graph extension on LOCOMO; this structured study does not reproduce it.

title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
finding: A-MEM dynamically links structured notes and evolves memory representations; no comparison to its implementation is claimed.

title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
finding: The cleaned original LongMemEval corpus was evaluated here using passage retrieval and lexical/adapted-judge proxies. Official evaluator reproduction and interactive online-memory validation remain future work.

title: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
finding: Agent Laboratory stages literature review, experimentation and report writing. This system borrows workflow design ideas, not source code.

title: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation
finding: AI-Researcher orchestrates scientific investigation and manuscript preparation; its research/writing boundary informs our design.

title: EvidentialRAG: Quantifying and Mitigating Information Conflict in Multi-Source Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Evidential Deep Learning
finding: Primary record identifies ERAG: claim support becomes Dirichlet evidence; conflict-preserving Dempster-Shafer fusion represents unresolved disagreement as uncertainty, which routes answering or abstention.
relevance: Direct comparison for uncertainty-aware conflict handling. Preserving conflicting records in a context is not implementation of evidential fusion or calibrated abstention.

title: ArbGraph: Conflict-Aware Evidence Arbitration for Reliable Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation
finding: Primary abstract describes atomic claims, support/contradiction graph edges, and iterative credibility propagation before generation.
relevance: Direct comparison for pre-generation arbitration; atomic record-group packing does not reproduce claim extraction or graph arbitration.

title: MemFlow: Intent-Driven Memory Orchestration for Small Language Model Agents
finding: Review's bounded-context orchestration description matches this primary record: intent routing, three retrieval/reasoning tiers, tier-dependent context budgets, and optional validation/retry.
relevance: Compare context construction and routing costs on shared tasks. MemFlow is an overloaded name; this identity excludes optical-flow, video-generation and systems-memory projects.

title: Verifiable Memory: Learning Unified Memory Management with Local and Global Verifiers for Large Language Model Agents
finding: VerMem learns a unified memory-operation policy with supervised initialization and reinforcement learning; local transition and global coherence verifiers supply training signals. Verifiers are used only during training.
relevance: Comparison concerns learned memory management and verification. A conflict-aware answer prompt is not the trained VerMem policy or its verifiers.

title: Decoupling Memory from Context: Structured Memory for Token-Efficient Test-Time Continual Learning
finding: This paper explicitly names its system GraphMemory: a graph of reusable strategies retrieved as query-relevant subgraphs under bounded retrieval. Primary record revised 6 October 2026.
relevance: Review's graph-structured bounded-context description matches this system. GraphMemory is not the paper title and should not be silently substituted with a graph-memory survey or G-Memory.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Conflicting Evidence
finding: RAMDocs (Retrieval with Ambiguity and Misinformation in Documents) is a dataset introduced in this paper, jointly covering ambiguity, misinformation and noise.
relevance: External conflict benchmark candidate. It is not a distinct paper, not evidence of a completed local benchmark, and not a source of assumed bitemporal annotations.

title: EHR-RAG: Bridging Long-Horizon Structured Electronic Health Records and Large Language Models via Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation
finding: Primary abstract describes event/time-aware hybrid retrieval, adaptive iterative retrieval, and factual/counterfactual evidence paths for structured longitudinal EHR prediction.
relevance: Cross-domain temporal retrieval comparison. This source does not establish clinical validity or dual valid-time/observation-time semantics for the local selector.

title: MiniLM: Deep Self-Attention Distillation for Task-Agnostic Compression of Pre-Trained Transformers
finding: Foundational self-attention distillation paper, not sufficient identity for sentence-embedding weights. Publisher/maintainer model cards establish the separate encoder provenance below.
relevance: Local dense retrieval uses a pretrained sentence encoder from the MiniLM family. No distillation training or original MiniLM experiments were reproduced here.
implementation_scope: Pretrained encoder inference component only, as inspected in research/advanced_retrieval.py; this audit did not execute inference or validate scores.

model_identity.local_pooling: attention-mask mean followed by L2 normalization
model_identity.naming_note: The sentence encoder's v2 suffix is not evidence that the distinct MiniLMv2 paper is its identity. Base card describes a six-layer model retaining alternate layers from microsoft/MiniLM-L12-H384-uncased.

title: Reciprocal rank fusion outperforms condorcet and individual rank learning methods
finding: Author-affiliated Google Research record verifies title, authors, SIGIR 2009 and pages 758-759; publisher search metadata verifies DOI. Direct ACM page fetch returned HTTP 403.
relevance: Local hybrid ranking adds reciprocal ranks from BM25 and dense lists with k=60 and equal weights; this is an established fusion component, not a new retrieval algorithm.
implementation_scope: rank_texts hybrid branch in research/advanced_retrieval.py: sum(1/(60+rank)), ranks starting at 1. No original SIGIR evaluation was reproduced by this audit.
